quotes.text: This guide only describes subscription management. If you’re setting up subscription purchases, see
If you use the customer portal with Stripe Connect, configure it for your platform, not a connected account.

To use different portal settings for different groups of customers, or to manage configurations for connected accounts as a *Connect* (Connect is Stripe's solution for multi-party businesses, such as marketplace or software platforms, to route payments between sellers, customers, and other recipients) platform, [create portal configurations with the API](https://docs.stripe.com/api/customer_portal/configurations/create.md):
When a customer wants to make changes to their subscription, generate a URL for the portal page using their Stripe customer ID through the portal session API.
Make sure you handle all events necessary to accurately monitor the statuses of the subscriptions you’ve configured.

findings: Both same-URL captures describe iOS digital-goods subscription management through a Stripe-hosted customer portal opened in Safari. They explicitly exclude subscription purchase flow, user authentication, and StoreKit native purchases (new raw:5-32; old raw:4-31). The US/EEA Apple Pay external-page sentence is context for a separate purchase guide, not permission or implementation detail for every app.

Both captures require portal configuration separately in sandbox and live mode. In this Connect flow, configure the portal for the platform rather than as the connected account (new raw:40; old raw:39). Adjacent text expressly allows the Connect platform to use the API to manage multiple portal configurations for its connected accounts or different customer groups (new raw:42-48; old raw:41-55). Product catalog setup is required for upgrade, downgrade, or quantity changes but not invoicing-only use (new raw:50-60; old raw:57-65). Tax-ID collection is optional in the stated Stripe Tax context; preview/testing require sandbox context and Dashboard edit permission (new raw:62-78; old raw:67-79).

The portal session URL is created server-side using the customer's Stripe customer ID and a return_url; the app calls its server, opens the returned URL in Safari, and uses universal links plus a fallback return page for navigation (new raw:156-179,185-245; old raw:158-180,184-244). The sample's placeholder customer lookup is not proof of an authentication or authorization implementation.

Both captures say production should have a webhook endpoint subscribed to appropriate event types and should handle all events needed to monitor configured subscription statuses; created, updated, and deleted are examples (new raw:276-280; old raw:275-279). The Node sample only branches on created and deleted and maps them directly to true/false without inspecting status (new raw:320-334; old raw:319-333). The current source:48-50 turns these simplified event branches into a general action table; created alone does not prove active access, and updated events need actual status handling.

The diff changes the guide's sample setup language and installation choices (Node install to Ruby gem, removes CocoaPods steps, expands CLI install/login), reformats code and lists, and changes image or reference links (diff:1-393). These are documentation/example changes; the portal session, customer identity, universal-link, configuration, and webhook lifecycle rules remain substantively the same. Removal of CocoaPods instructions here does not establish SDK deprecation.
historical_claims_to_preserve: Retain the older capture as dated evidence of the management-only flow, portal session customer ID, Safari opening, universal-link return/fallback, and webhook-based subscription monitoring (old raw:17-30,158-244,275-279; new raw:18-31,156-245,276-280).

Retain both adjacent Connect statements: configure this portal for the platform, not as a connected account (old raw:39; new raw:40), while a Connect platform may manage differentiated configurations for its connected accounts through the API (old raw:41-55; new raw:42-48). Do not collapse either into a platform-only prohibition on platform-managed connected-account configurations.
Retain the sandbox/edit-permission preview limit, optional tax-ID setting, product-catalog condition, and webhook event completeness requirement (old raw:59-79,277-279; new raw:52-78,278-280).
conflicts: Current source wiki/sources/source-stripe-inapp-digital-goods-customer-portal.md:54 says only 'Configure portal for the platform, not a connected account'; wiki/concepts/stripe-inapp-payments.md:109 and wiki/stripe-index.md:124 compress this to 'platform only.' Both captures give the platform configuration instruction (old raw:39; new raw:40) and an adjacent API option for a Connect platform to manage portal configurations for connected accounts (old raw:41; new raw:42). Qualify all three labels with that platform-managed API option. This does not mean connected accounts themselves configure the portal.

Current wiki/sources/source-stripe-inapp-digital-goods-customer-portal.md:48 instructs 'customer.subscription.created | Mark subscription active' as a general rule. Both captures make that direct mapping only inside a simplified Node example (old raw:319-333; new raw:320-334), while the guide says to handle all events necessary to accurately monitor subscription statuses (old raw:277; new raw:278). Correct the table to inspect the subscription's actual status before granting active access; created alone is not an active-status guarantee.

Current source:49 says updated events handle pause/upgrade/cancel changes, but the example has no updated branch; distinguish the documented event name and required comprehensive status monitoring from illustrative code that implements only created/deleted (old raw:277,319-333; new raw:278,320-334).

Current source:39 groups product name, description, and quantity restrictions as editable without retaining that quantity restrictions are Dashboard-editable while names and descriptions are editable in Dashboard and API (old raw:63-65; new raw:58-60). Keep that distinction if this detail remains in the source.
unresolved_questions: The linked subscription webhook guide and lifecycle references were navigation only for this job; the assigned page alone does not enumerate every status transition or prove a given customer's entitlement state.
The changed SDK installation snippets do not establish whether CocoaPods or the old Node setup remains supported; no package or platform compatibility check was performed.

answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/mobile/digital-goods/customer-portal, both captures describe subscription management from an iOS app: create a portal session on the server for the Stripe customer, open its URL in Safari, provide a universal-link return and fallback, and use webhooks for status monitoring (new raw:156-179,185-245,276-280; old raw:158-180,184-244,275-279). [[source-stripe-inapp-digital-goods-customer-portal]] separates management from purchases. For Connect, configure this flow's portal for the platform, while the platform may manage differentiated configurations for connected accounts using the API (new raw:40-42; old raw:39-41); connected accounts are not instructed to configure it themselves. Product catalog setup is conditional on plan or quantity changes (new raw:52-54; old raw:59).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/mobile/digital-goods/customer-portal, the same-URL diff changes setup examples, code formatting, and navigation, without changing the portal lifecycle (old raw:17-30,158-180,275-279; new raw:18-31,156-179,276-280). [[source-stripe-inapp-digital-goods-customer-portal]] needs two bounded existing-claim corrections. Its webhook table at lines 48-50 treats a simplified created/deleted true/false sample as a general active-status rule, despite the guide requiring all events needed for accurate status (old raw:277,319-333; new raw:278,320-334). Its Connect note at line 54, the in-app concept label, and Stripe index label should retain platform configuration while adding the platform-managed API option for connected-account configurations (old raw:39-41; new raw:40-42).
